At last, some composure returned. I groaned.
Precious time, gone. That much required no calculation.

I had to move now.
The tsurugi—that tsurugi was out of the question.

Touching it had been a mistake.
It would bring calamity. On this point I had no doubt to offer, no 'perhaps' to hide behind.

...And Hikaru had put on something like it.
Why had I not stopped her?

Even that was not the end of the worry.
What had happened in the fight? The bandits had far greater numbers. Armored warrior or not, Hikaru could not have found that easy.

Thinking more only made the urgency worse.
...Enough. I had to go into town and look.

First, find out whether Hikaru was safe.

The half-ruined sanctuary would have to remain half-ruined. Nothing I could do for it now.
Move my foster mother somewhere safe, and then—
